gap_finder.diagnosis: The scores are disconnected from the matched-data comparison, and the ending overstates evaluation scope.
gap_finder.reader_question: Does layout coverage help at fixed demonstration count, and where was that tested?

proposer.operation: Frame the comparison around coverage at fixed data volume; bind both scores to their policies and the same held-out layouts; narrow the interpretation to this test.
proposer.expected_effect: The reader can identify what the comparison distinguishes without inferring that more demonstrations explain the advantage.
proposer.risk: Calling the comparison proof of generalization would exceed the evidence; listing every controlled detail could obscure the contrast.
proposer.success_test: From prose alone, recover the fixed count, varied coverage, comparison scope, direction and bounded implication.

writer.text: To test layout coverage at fixed data volume, we train both policies on 600 demonstrations with the same architecture, task mix and optimization budget. Training across 12 layouts yields 68% mean success on six held-out layouts, compared with 51% for training on two layouts. This comparison supports broader training-layout coverage for the evaluated layout shift; it does not establish robustness to other tasks or shifts.
